# @zakkster/lite-headless

VERSION 1.4.0

58 headless UI primitives on signal-based reactivity (@zakkster/lite-signal).
Zero styling. Tree-shakable via per-primitive subpath exports. Framework-
agnostic. Every primitive ships an optional `<lite-*>` custom element.

The catalog spans overlays (dialog, alert-dialog, popover, tooltip, hover-card,
menu, combobox, command-palette, toast, drawer, tour), form controls (button,
slider, switch, rating, pin-input, tag-input, file-upload, color-picker,
date-picker, stepper, inline-edit, form-field, password-input), data/display (tabs,
accordion, tree, table-less primitives, pagination, carousel, calendar, kanban,
sortable, timeline, descriptions, stat, meter, progress, skeleton, breadcrumb,
badge, tag, avatar, card, banner, result, empty-state, separator, clipboard,
notification-center), and layout/util (affix, anchor, back-top, split-panels,
toolbar, toggle-group, steps, radio-group, picture).

## Architecture

The overlay primitives compose shared layers from /src/_overlay/:
- core: state machine, open + status signals, cleanup ledger
- position: 12 placements + flip + shift + arrow + autoUpdate
- dismiss: Escape stack + composedPath-aware outside-click
- focus: trap (modal) or move-only (non-modal); inert/visibility-aware
- portal: move + restore across containers
- scroll-lock: refcounted body overflow
- aria: id generation + attribute setters

Non-overlay primitives reuse only the aria id helpers. Every primitive returns
a handle with `attach*(el)` methods + `destroy()`; overlays additionally expose
`open`, `status`, `setOpen`, `toggle`.

## hover-card: the lite-floating integration

hover-card is positioned by @zakkster/lite-floating (createFloating +
bindTransform + offset/flip/shift), whose autoUpdate pulls in
@zakkster/lite-observe transitively. The other overlays keep _overlay/position
(exact-pixel test contract). lite-floating + lite-observe are OPTIONAL peers --
needed only if you use hover-card or the floating-adapter subpath. The
lite-floating floor is ^1.1.0: its 1.1.0 pool-returns disposed positioner
signals (H-12 seal pattern), which the torture churn relies on.

## Subpaths

Pattern: `@zakkster/lite-headless/<name>` (factory) and
`@zakkster/lite-headless/<name>/element` (registers `<lite-<name>>`). The bare
`@zakkster/lite-headless` re-exports every createXxx factory. Each primitive
also ships its own `llms.txt` next to its source with the full options table,
API, and painted-attribute contract.

Opt-in subpath `@zakkster/lite-headless/floating-adapter` exports
`createFloatingPositioner(options?)` -> a `(spec) -> {update, autoUpdate,
destroy}` positioner factory backed by @zakkster/lite-floating. Pass it as the
`positioner` option of tooltip/popover/combobox/menu to route placement through
lite-floating (identical spec + 12-placement vocabulary). Middleware built once
per open; autoUpdate is a no-op (lite-floating owns it); element boundary throws.

Newest additions: separator, clipboard, password-input, alert-dialog, hover-card.

## Peer dependencies

- @zakkster/lite-signal   (required)
- @zakkster/lite-element  (optional; only for */element subpaths)
- @zakkster/lite-floating (optional, ^1.1.0; hover-card + floating-adapter)
- @zakkster/lite-observe  (optional; pulled transitively by lite-floating)

## Conventions

- Static config (set once at createXxx). Reactive state is exposed via signals.
- Unknown option keys throw TypeError at construction with a did-you-mean hint; null and non-objects are rejected; no-arg/undefined is legal.
- tooltip/popover/combobox/menu accept a pluggable `positioner` factory
  (`(spec) -> {update, autoUpdate, destroy}`); undefined selects the built-in
  _overlay/position engine. The engine is resolved once at construction (no
  per-tick branch on the default path); a non-function throws at construction
  and a handle missing update/autoUpdate/destroy throws at first open. The
  floating-adapter subpath supplies a lite-floating-backed factory.
- status ReadSignal: 'closed' -> 'opening' -> 'open' -> 'closing' -> 'closed'
- Slots use data-* attributes: data-trigger, data-content, data-anchor,
  data-arrow, data-close, data-trigger, data-indicator, data-input, data-toggle
- aria attributes managed automatically
- transition:true makes status wait for transitionend; default is immediate
- Teardown/callback throws are swallowed by design: destroy() runs every
  cleanup even if one throws, onOpenChange/finalize throws cannot corrupt the
  state machine, and addCleanup after destroy runs immediately.
- destroy() returns every factory-owned lite-signal node to the registry pool
  (H-12), including per-item nodes (kanban column order, file-upload entry
  progress, radio-group item disabled) on their removal paths. Churned
  create/destroy cycles therefore run indefinitely on lite-signal's default
  fixed 1024-node registry. Owned signals are SEALED, not just disposed
  (src/_overlay/seal.js): a destroyed handle's accessors keep answering the
  frozen final value (writes stay no-ops; subscribe fires once with the final
  value). Consumer-supplied controlled signals are never disposed.
- Status is generation-guarded: a superseded finalize (same-tick open<->close
  toggle) never emits a stale status such as an illegal closing->open flash.
- Escape dismisses the most-recently-OPENED overlay (global open-sequence
  stamp), not the most-recently-bound; defaultOpen overlays rank lowest.
- CSS contract: see docs/CSS_CONTRACT.md (taxonomy) and
  docs/CSS_CONTRACT_APPENDIX.md (per-primitive, auto-generated)

## Test stack

- node:test (NOT vitest)
- happy-dom devDep (pinned ^15.11.0)
- Per-test setupDOM/teardownDOM; teardown calls window.happyDOM.close()
- 1607 tests; types.d.ts declares the documented surface (`tsc --noEmit`), while `test/api-surface.test.js` pins the full JS export surface against api-surface-snapshot.json (`npm run api:update` to regenerate); the undocumented allowlist is empty and the gate enforces that every live export is declared in its own subpath's `declare module` block -- the sole attribution rule is that for the bare "." specifier a file-top-level declaration (VERSION) counts as the barrel's own
